toc.title: Responding to spoken prompts with a multimodal model

html:
1A text analysis application

To analyze text in code you use Azure Language through a client library. The pattern is the same as other Foundry Tools: a client with an endpoint and a credential, one call, read the result.

Step What the code does
1. Create the resource A Language (Foundry Tool) resource gives an endpoint and a key
2. Create the client TextAnalyticsClient with the endpoint and an AzureKeyCredential
3. Send documents A list of text strings
4. Call the feature For example analyze_sentiment
5. Read the result Overall sentiment, sentence results, confidence scores 
import os
from azure.ai.textanalytics import TextAnalyticsClient
from azure.core.credentials import AzureKeyCredential

language_key = os.environ.get("LANGUAGE_KEY")
language_endpoint = os.environ.get("LANGUAGE_ENDPOINT")

client = TextAnalyticsClient(endpoint=language_endpoint, credential=AzureKeyCredential(language_key))

documents = ["The food and service were unacceptable. The concierge was nice, however."]
result = client.analyze_sentiment(documents, show_opinion_mining=True)
Line Meaning
pip install azure-ai-textanalytics==5.2.0 The package used in the quickstart
os.environ.get(...) Reads the key and endpoint from environment variables, not from the code
TextAnalyticsClient(...) The client for text analysis features
documents = [...] The input: a list of texts
analyze_sentiment(..., show_opinion_mining=True) Sentiment plus opinions about specific targets

The sample result for that text is an overall sentiment of Mixed, with a result for each sentence. Other methods in the same client cover key phrase extraction, entity recognition, language detection and PII detection. [Verify live] for current package names and versions.

Exam tip

. A text analysis app uses a key and endpoint (or Entra ID), a client object, and one method per feature. The method name tells the feature: analyze_sentiment, extract_key_phrases, recognize_entities, detect_language. Beyond the study guide for the last three names.

2Speech applications with Azure Speech

Azure Speech in Foundry Tools gives speech recognition, speech synthesis and translation. In Python you use the Speech SDK package azure-cognitiveservices-speech.

import os
import azure.cognitiveservices.speech as speechsdk

speech_config = speechsdk.SpeechConfig(subscription=os.environ.get('SPEECH_KEY'), endpoint=os.environ.get('ENDPOINT'))
speech_config.speech_recognition_language = "en-US"

audio_config = speechsdk.audio.AudioConfig(use_default_microphone=True)
speech_recognizer = speechsdk.SpeechRecognizer(speech_config=speech_config, audio_config=audio_config)

speech_recognition_result = speech_recognizer.recognize_once_async().get()
Line Meaning
SpeechConfig(subscription=..., endpoint=...) Connects to the Speech resource with a key and endpoint
speech_recognition_language = "en-US" The spoken language to recognize
AudioConfig(use_default_microphone=True) Where the audio comes from: the microphone. For a file use AudioConfig(filename="YourAudioFile.wav")
SpeechRecognizer(...) The object that turns speech into text
recognize_once_async().get() Recognizes one utterance (up to about 30 seconds, or until silence) and returns the result

For text to speech the SDK uses a speech synthesizer with a voice you choose, and SSML can adjust pitch, rate and volume. Beyond the study guide for the class name.

Exam tip

. AudioConfig says where audio comes from or goes to (microphone, speaker, file). SpeechConfig says which resource and language or voice. Recognizer = speech to text; synthesizer = text to speech.

3Responding to spoken prompts with a multimodal model

A multimodal model can accept more than text: some deployed models accept audio (spoken prompts) as input and can reply in text or speech. There are two designs:

Design How it works When
Pipeline Speech to text (Azure Speech) → text model → text to speech (Azure Speech) You want control of each step and a choice of voice
Audio-capable multimodal model You send the spoken prompt (audio) directly to a deployed model that supports audio input and read its reply Simpler flow, fewer parts; needs a model deployed with audio support

The model must be deployed in your project (Module 7), and your app uses the deployment name like any other model call. Which models support audio input changes often, so always check the model's capabilities in the catalog. [Verify live]

Exam tip

. "Respond to a spoken question" → either speech to text + model + text to speech or an audio-capable multimodal model. The deciding word is "deployed multimodal model": it takes audio in without a separate transcription step.

4Exam Q&A

4.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer)

S1Fabrikam Outdoors writes a program that sends customer reviews to Azure Language and prints whether each is positive or negative. Which call fits?

  • Aanalyze_sentiment
  • Brecognize_once_async
  • Cbegin_analyze
  • Dimages.generate
Show the answer

Answer: A. analyze_sentiment is the text analysis method for sentiment.

S2Where should the program read the Language key and endpoint from, to avoid hard-coding secrets?

  • AEnvironment variables
  • BThe review text itself
  • CThe prompt sent to the model
  • DThe playground of the portal
Show the answer

Answer: A. The quickstart reads the key and endpoint from environment variables.

S3In the speech sample, which object decides that the audio comes from the microphone?

  • ASpeechConfig language
  • BThe recognizer's result
  • CThe subscription name
  • DAudioConfig
Show the answer

Answer: D. AudioConfig defines the audio source, here the default microphone.

S4Which object turns spoken audio into text?

  • ATextAnalyticsClient
  • BAIProjectClient
  • CPromptAgentDefinition
  • DSpeechRecognizer
Show the answer

Answer: D. The speech recognizer performs speech-to-text.

S5A team wants users to speak a question and hear a spoken answer, using one text model. Which pipeline fits?

  • AObject detection of the audio, then OCR of the result
  • BKey phrase extraction only, with no speech steps
  • CImage generation only, with no speech steps
  • DSpeech to text, then the text model, then text to speech
Show the answer

Answer: D. Recognition converts speech to text for the model, and synthesis speaks the answer.

S6What does a deployed multimodal model that supports audio input allow?

  • AChanging the Azure region of the project
  • BSending the spoken prompt directly to the model
  • CDeleting the system prompt of the model to save tokens
  • DSkipping authentication to save time on every call
Show the answer

Answer: B. An audio-capable multimodal model accepts audio as input without a separate transcription step.

4.2 Recall questions

R1Which client class is used for text analysis in the sample?

Show the answer

TextAnalyticsClient.

R2What does show_opinion_mining add?

Show the answer

Opinions linked to specific targets in the text.

R3What does SpeechConfig hold?

Show the answer

The Speech resource key and endpoint, and the language or voice.

R4Which object defines microphone or file input?

Show the answer

AudioConfig.

R5How long can recognize_once_async listen?

Show the answer

Up to about 30 seconds, or until silence is detected.

R6What does SSML adjust?

Show the answer

Pitch, pronunciation, speaking rate and volume of synthesized speech.
